summary:
We developed the frontend of HexaFlare, an interactive interface with:

->A 3D Earth and satellite map view with hexagonal zones across Bangladesh, plus detailed views of the Rajshahi and Chattogram divisions

->A telemetry panel for each zone showing detection counts, Fire Radiative Power, and the MODIS/VIIRS sensor breakdown

->A daily heat map and 12-month calendar for comparing current activity with past patterns

->An alert registration interface where users choose an area and a threshold

MODIS and VIIRS observe fires at different resolutions and over different periods, so their detections are hard to compare directly. HexaFlare's design brings both into a single hexagonal grid, so each zone has one consistent activity level while still showing how much each sensor contributed. This makes the two datasets easier to interpret side by side.

Fire activity can escalate quickly, and raw satellite data is hard for most people to read. HexaFlare shows how that data can become clear and actionable: a simple map, a comparison against past patterns, and alerts for the areas people care about. This could help communities, local authorities, and researchers notice unusual fire activity earlier.
details:
What exactly does it do?
It shows NASA MODIS and VIIRS fire detections as colour-coded hexagons across Bangladesh’s 64 districts, on a 3D globe and satellite map. Clicking a zone shows its detections, fire radiative power and sensor breakdown.

How does it work?
A script cleans the NASA FIRMS data, and the app places both sensors on one hexagon grid with a single activity level per zone. Users can register an area, and the app sends an email through EmailJS when it reaches their chosen level.

What benefits does it have?
Raw satellite data becomes a simple map, both sensors appear in one view, and alerts let people follow only their own areas.

What do you hope to achieve?
To help communities and local authorities notice fires earlier and respond to their air quality and health effects.

Tools used
JavaScript, React, Vite, globe.gl, three.js, Leaflet, H3, Recharts, EmailJS, Node.js, and NASA FIRMS data. It runs on a normal laptop with a browser.
